title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 9: faith foreseen before obtaining crown, not before destinating it
pass_a_gloss: Foresight therefore was had of the faith and patience of Stephen as antecedent to the obtaining itself of the crown; but it was not foreseen as antecedent to the destination of this crown. For the divine foresight of that measure of grace which he bestowed on Stephen, and which he exercised so gloriously, was founded in the preceding decree of election; and the decree itself of election to so great a glory was not [founded] in foresight of the faith which he was about to receive from God and afterward to display in the combat.
pass_b_english: So Stephen's faith and patience were foreseen as going before his actually receiving the crown — not as going before the destinating of that crown. Divine foresight of the measure of grace God gave him, and which he exercised so gloriously, rested on the prior decree of election; the decree electing him to that glory did not rest on foresight of the faith he would receive from God and later show in the fight.
source_text: Praevisa igitur fuit fides et patientia Stephani ut antecedens ipsam coronae adeptionem; sed non fuit praevisa ut antecedens hujus coronae destinationem. Nam praescientia Divina de illa gratiae mensura quam largitus est Stephano, quamque ille exercuit tam gloriose, fundata fuit in praecedente decreto electionis; et non ipsum decretum electionis ad tantam gloriam, in praescientia fidei, quam accepturus a Deo et in certamine postmodum exseruit, fuit.
notes: Densify De praedestinatione Cap. III Rat. 9 section 315. Pass A!=B. Packet praedestinatione_cap3_rat9_densify. Honest partial.
